chosen.premise: Scyther has the Flying type, yet its Pokédex says it very rarely spreads its wings to fly.
chosen.hook: Scyther is Flying-type—but almost never flies.
chosen.visualIdea: Display the Flying typing beside grounded ninja-like dashes, ending with folded wings instead of takeoff.
chosen.note: Excellent type-versus-behavior contradiction, clearly sourced and easy to show; the Flying typing versus folded wings creates an immediate visual hook.

candidates.premise: Scyther can evolve down two radically different paths: Steel with a traded Metal Coat or Rock with Black Augurite.
candidates.hook: Scyther has two evolutions—and the item changes everything.
candidates.visualIdea: Split Scyther down the middle: one route becomes Bug/Steel Scizor, the other Bug/Rock Kleavor.
candidates.note: Highly specific to Scyther’s branching evolution and visually powerful, with radically different Bug/Steel and Bug/Rock outcomes. The evolution methods are supported by the cited trusted-secondary research.

candidates.premise: Scyther's scythes become sharper through battle and cutting hard objects, eventually felling a massive tree in one slice.
candidates.hook: Scyther can literally sharpen its weapons by fighting.
candidates.visualIdea: Show dull scythes cutting hard material, then sharpened blades dropping a massive tree with one swing.
candidates.note: A concrete progression with a strong payoff: battles and cutting hard objects sharpen the scythes, culminating in felling a massive tree.

candidates.premise: Scyther moves so fast that its opponents can see an illusion of multiple Scythers.
candidates.hook: How can one Scyther look like an entire squad?
candidates.visualIdea: One Scyther blurs across the screen, leaving several afterimages that vanish when it stops.
candidates.note: Strongly tied to Scyther’s signature speed and directly supported by multiple entries, but the basic afterimage idea is already familiar to fans.

candidates.premise: Young Scyther live together in deep mountains, training both their scythe fighting and high-speed movement.
candidates.hook: Scyther's ninja skills begin as group training in the mountains.
candidates.visualIdea: Show young Scyther training in formation, practicing blade swings before dissolving into high-speed blurs.
candidates.note: The group mountain training is supported, but calling it a formal origin of ninja skills overreaches the entries, which only describe shared combat and speed training.

rounds.request: No stronger angle is required; this one has the clearest contradiction, strongest visual treatment, and complete research support.
